test_title: PYST 17: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 12 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In October 2024, the Mediation Act, 2023 came into force. What is a key feature introduced by this legislation?

options.text: It replaces arbitration and conciliation with mediation as the sole dispute resolution method.
It mandates that all mediation proceedings must be conducted only by retired judges.
It abolishes the role of mediators in public sector disputes.
It makes mediation compulsory for all civil and commercial disputes before court proceedings.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It makes mediation compulsory for all civil and commercial disputes before court proceedings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Mediation Act, 2023 introduces **mandatory pre-litigation mediation** for civil and commercial disputes, aiming to reduce the burden on courts.
 
• This legislation promotes a **time-bound dispute resolution mechanism**, ensuring faster settlements through mediation.
 
• The Act establishes a **Mediation Council of India** to regulate the conduct of mediators and mediation institutions.
 
• It provides legal recognition to **mediated settlement agreements**, making them enforceable as court decrees.
 
• The Act encourages participation of trained mediators, ensuring professional and impartial facilitation in dispute resolution processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mediation:**

 
 
• Mediation is a voluntary and collaborative process where disputing parties work with a neutral third party (mediator) to resolve their issues.
 
• It differs from arbitration as it does not involve binding decisions made by a third party.
 
 
 
• **Mediation Council of India:**
 
 
• Established under the Mediation Act, 2023, the council oversees the accreditation of mediators and mediation service providers.
 
• It aims to standardize mediation practices across India.
 
 
 
• **Mediated Settlement Agreements:**
 
 
• These agreements, reached through mediation, carry legal enforceability under the Act.
 
• They are treated as final and binding, similar to court decrees.
 
 
 
• **Pre-litigation Mediation:**
 
 
• This process requires disputing parties to attempt mediation before approaching the court.
 
• It helps in reducing litigation costs and court congestion.
